title: Bengaluru to Kalasa via Sakleshpur
blurb: Out of the city on NH75, past Hassan's temples, then into the Western Ghats: coffee estates around Sakleshpur and Mudigere and a long run of bends down into the Bhadra valley at Kalasa.
notes: Malnad roads are narrow and slippery in the monsoon (June to September), and forest stops have leeches.

title: Pollachi to Valparai
blurb: Flat coconut country to Aliyar dam, then forty numbered hairpins up the Anamalai hills, with Monkey Falls and Loam's View on the way and tea estates rolling over the top to Valparai.
notes: Elephants and lion-tailed macaques cross the ghat road; the Aliyar check post logs every vehicle.

title: Mysuru to Ooty via Gudalur
blurb: Through the Bandipur and Mudumalai forests, where elephants often stand by the road, then the long Naduvattam ghat from Gudalur up into the Nilgiris.
notes: The Bandipur and Mudumalai stretch is closed to traffic from 9 pm to 6 am.

title: Mangaluru to Chikkamagaluru via Charmadi Ghat
blurb: From the coast across the plains to Ujire, then the Charmadi ghat: a steep, forested climb of tight bends and waterfalls up to the coffee hills.
notes: Charmadi closes to heavy vehicles, and sometimes to all traffic, after monsoon landslides.

title: Udupi to Shivamogga via Agumbe
blurb: Temple town to the Agumbe ghat, a short climb of hairpins through rainforest to one of India's wettest villages and its sunset point, then down through the Malnad to Shivamogga.
notes: The ghat is narrow and closed to heavy vehicles in the monsoon.

title: Mumbai to Goa along the Konkan coast
blurb: The long way south: Konkan villages, sea forts, beaches and river crossings by Ratnagiri and Malvan before the road reaches Goa.
notes: Highway widening is still going on in places; the coastal stretches near Ratnagiri and Malvan are slower but quieter.

title: Pune to Kolad via Tamhini Ghat
blurb: A short monsoon favourite: past Mulshi lake and over Tamhini ghat, where the road runs under waterfalls, down to the Kundalika river at Kolad.
notes: At its best in the rains; go on a weekday to miss the crowds.

title: Mumbai to Malshej Ghat
blurb: Out past Kalyan and Murbad to the cliffs of Malshej, where the road climbs the Sahyadri wall between waterfalls and cloud.
notes: Landslides can close the ghat for days in heavy rain; check before you ride.

title: Chennai to Puducherry by the East Coast Road
blurb: The East Coast Road runs between the Bay of Bengal and backwaters, past the shore temples of Mamallapuram, to the French quarter of Puducherry.
notes: Ride early: the road fills with traffic by mid-morning at weekends.

title: Kochi to Munnar
blurb: From the backwaters through rubber and spice country to Adimali, then up into the tea gardens and waterfalls of the Kannan Devan hills.
notes: Mist cuts visibility on the ghat in the evenings, especially in the monsoon.

title: Madurai to Kodaikanal
blurb: Temple city to hill station: across the plains to Batlagundu, then the ghat climbs nearly two kilometres up the Palani hills through bends, viewpoints and pine forest.
notes: Use engine braking on the long way down.

title: Bengaluru to Madikeri
blurb: Past Mysuru to Kushalnagar's Tibetan settlement, then up into Kodagu: coffee, pepper and misty bends to Madikeri.
notes: The last climb to Madikeri is narrow; watch for buses on the bends.

title: Kolhapur to Goa via Amboli Ghat
blurb: Sugarcane country to the edge of the Sahyadris at Amboli, where the road drops past waterfalls in the fog to Sawantwadi and on to Goa.
notes: Amboli is at its best in the monsoon, with fog and waterfalls by the road.

title: Hyderabad to Srisailam
blurb: South through the Deccan to the Nallamala hills, then forest road through the Amrabad tiger reserve to the Krishna gorge and the temple town of Srisailam.
notes: The road through the tiger reserve is closed from 9 pm to 6 am.

title: Manali to Leh
blurb: The classic high-altitude ride: through the Atal Tunnel into Lahaul, past Keylong and Sarchu, and over the high passes of the Zanskar range down to Leh.
notes: Open roughly June to October. The passes are above 5,000 m: acclimatise a day at Keylong or Jispa, and carry fuel for the long stretch without pumps after Tandi. The elevation profile reads the hill above the Atal Tunnel, so it shows a bump there.

title: Shimla to Kaza through Kinnaur
blurb: Apple orchards at Narkanda, then the Sutlej gorge through Kinnaur on roads cut into cliffs, past Nako's lake into the cold desert of Spiti.
notes: Landslides are common around Malling and Nako, and the road beyond Reckong Peo is partly unpaved.

title: Jaipur to Jaisalmer
blurb: Across Rajasthan from the Pink City by Ajmer and the blue city of Jodhpur, the land drying into dunes before Jaisalmer's golden fort.
notes: Very hot from April to June; carry water, and fill up in Jodhpur and Pokaran.

title: Guwahati to Tawang via Sela Pass
blurb: Over the Brahmaputra plains to Tezpur, then up into Arunachal by Bomdila and Dirang and over Sela Pass at 4,170 m to the monastery town of Tawang.
notes: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit for Arunachal Pradesh; Sela Pass can close with snow in winter.

title: Siliguri to Darjeeling
blurb: From the plains straight up the Himalayan foothills by Kurseong, sharing the bends with the toy train, to tea gardens and a view of Kanchenjunga.
notes: Hill Cart Road shares its bends with the toy train; Rohini Road is the quicker climb.

title: Rishikesh to Chopta
blurb: Up the Ganga by Devprayag and Rudraprayag, then the Mandakini valley to Ukhimath and the meadows of Chopta below Tungnath, the highest Shiva temple.
notes: Monsoon landslides often close the Badrinath highway; snow can block Chopta in winter. The road ends at Chopta, below the temple.

title: Bengaluru to Mullayanagiri
blurb: To Chikkamagaluru's coffee estates, then the narrow road up the Baba Budan range to Mullayanagiri, Karnataka's highest peak.
notes: The last stretch is single-lane; private vehicles may be stopped at weekends and on holidays.

title: Kozhikode to Wayanad via the Thamarassery Ghat
blurb: From the Malabar coast up the Thamarassery Ghat, nine hairpins from Adivaram to the Lakkidi viewpoint, onto the Wayanad plateau at Kalpetta.
notes: The ghat jams on weekend evenings, and heavy monsoon rain closes it now and then.

title: Leh to Nubra Valley over Khardung La
blurb: Up from Leh in loops to Khardung La at about 5,350 m, one of the highest roads riders can take, and down to the sand dunes and monastery of Diskit in the Nubra Valley.
notes: Nubra needs an Inner Line Permit. Spend two days in Leh first: the pass is over 5,300 m.

title: Leh to Pangong Tso over Chang La
blurb: East from Leh past Karu, over Chang La at about 5,360 m, through Tangtse and along the long blue lake of Pangong Tso to Spangmik.
notes: Pangong needs an Inner Line Permit. Streams can flood the road on summer afternoons; cross early.

title: Srinagar to Leh over Zoji La
blurb: From the Kashmir valley by Sonamarg over Zoji La, then through Drass and Kargil and over Namika La and Fotu La to Leh: the classic way into Ladakh.
notes: Zoji La opens from about May to November; near the top the road is broken and muddy, and it closes for snow.

title: Shillong to Sohra (Cherrapunji)
blurb: South from Shillong across the rolling Khasi Hills to Sohra on the edge of the plateau, among the wettest places on earth, with waterfalls and living root bridges below.
notes: In the monsoon the falls are at their biggest, but the road is wet and often in cloud.

title: Gangtok to Tsomgo Lake
blurb: A steep climb from Gangtok on the road towards Nathu La, from forest to bare mountainside, to the glacial Tsomgo Lake at about 3,750 m.
notes: A permit is needed, arranged through a registered operator in Gangtok; private vehicles from outside Sikkim may be turned back.
